A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Number Token Loss work and retain the original mathematics benchmark. Their complete main texts and appendices support comparison of equations, experiments, tables and figures despite substantial expansion and reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original training and evaluation of T5, NTL variants, Regression Transformer and xVal on mathematics interpolation and extrapolation tests (Table 1).

after.justification: V2 retains original empirical results and adds experiments on regression, reading comprehension, multiplication, GSM8K, computational efficiency and several ablations.

M1.justification: The CE-plus-NTL framework and MSE branch remain, but v2 replaces the default Wasserstein CDF computation with a direct one-hot formulation that supports irregularly spaced, multi-digit tokens. It also introduces flexible transport costs and a tested cost-squashing variant (Sections 2 and 4.5; Algorithm A2). These extend the procedure beyond v1's digit-level formulation.

E1.justification: The original DeepMind mathematics coverage is retained. V2 additionally evaluates humor-score regression on rJokes, generative reading comprehension on MultiRC, GSM8K mathematical reasoning, and controlled multiplication scenarios, substantially broadening the represented tasks and data.

E2.justification: V2 adds Gaussian Cross Entropy comparisons (Tables 3 and A6), a T5 regression-head control (Table 4), and P10, P1000, B1999 and FP15 encoding comparisons (Table A1). The RT-plus-NTL-MSE comparator is removed from the retained mathematics comparison in Table 1.

E3.justification: The original mathematics splits and 1.05M-step budget remain. New protocols include 100,000-example T5-small ablations trained for 2.5M iterations, tokenizer controls, decoder-only model configurations, T5-3B evaluation, and MultiRC reformulated as answer generation. For the retained benchmark, v2 changes xVal accuracy from exact matching to matching predictions rounded to two decimal places.

E4.justification: V2 adds loss-weight and loss-family ablations, Gaussian smoothing and combination tests, tokenizer controls, runtime and sample-efficiency analyses, and GSM8K digit-boundary and error-distribution studies. Appendix Figures A2–A4 and Example 1 add generalization analyses, token-distribution evidence and a worked comparison beyond v1's limited analyses.

E5.justification: V1 reports point estimates without repeated-run uncertainty. V2 introduces means and standard deviations across runs for multiple evaluations, including four-run ablations. Some counts conflict: rJokes uses three runs in Section 4.3 and Appendix A.6.3, five in Table 4's caption, and four in Table 6's caption. These discrepancies limit interpretation but do not obscure the substantial reporting change.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive benchmark and analysis results, including GSM8K accuracy of 13.5% for CE versus 17.7% for NTL (Table 9). In corresponding Table 1, NTL-MAE entries replace RT-plus-NTL-MSE entries, and T5 extrapolation accuracy changes from 0.3686 to 0.367 beyond rounding. xVal's new 0.10/0.058 accuracies use the revised rounding criterion; Figure A1 still displays zero, creating an internal inconsistency.

T1.justification: V2 adds an optimal-transport definition with explicit token-distance costs, the one-hot reduction, and conditions for the CDF formulation (Equations 2–5). Appendix A.5 adds an algebraic normalization argument for xVal's incompatibility with T5. These substantially extend v1's directly stated loss formulas and informal normalization discussion.

C1.justification: Beyond v1's central claim of improved T5 mathematics performance, v2 explicitly claims compatibility with multi-digit tokenizers, performance comparable to a regression head, preservation of text-task performance, and effectiveness at billion-parameter scale. These broaden the contributions stated in the abstract, introduction and conclusion.

C2.justification: V2 adds substantive limitations concerning equal weighting of digit positions and instability from large multi-digit tokens, recommending digit-level tokenization. It also interprets accuracy–R2 discrepancies, task-dependent benefits of combining GCE with NTL, and generalization behavior. V1's explanation for the lack of benefit from adding NTL-MSE to RT is removed.

D1.justification: V2 expands Algorithm A2 and supplies task-specific training iterations, loss weights, subset sizes, module choices, MultiRC processing instructions and runtime-benchmark controls. Appendix A.6 adds A100 and A40 hardware alongside A6000. The original software version, core mathematics settings and repository link are retained; the additions substantially expand reproducibility information.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands its positioning through discussion of regression as classification, optimal transport, Gaussian label smoothing, decoding order, tokenizer direction and modular arithmetic. New references such as Shah and Aamodt, Stewart et al., Cuturi, and Wang et al. support substantive comparisons and distinctions beyond v1's narrower positioning.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction and conclusion, adds an explicit contribution list, separates experimental setup from the method, and organizes results around distinct claims. The appendices are reorganized into model descriptions and experiment-specific subsections. These are substantial narrative and structural changes.

P2.justification: The main text changes from single-column to two-column layout. V2 redraws and combines the NTL schematic and loss illustration, rearranges the loss heatmaps, and moves the original performance plot to Figure A1 with altered rows. Numerous new tables, runtime plots, generalization heatmaps and error-distribution figures substantially expand the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: V1's broad applicability and efficiency claims rested mainly on one T5 mathematics benchmark. V2 substantially strengthens their assessment through measured runtime, additional architectures and tasks, regression-head and tokenizer controls, repeated-run reporting, and explicit limitations. Conflicting run counts, table–figure discrepancies and removal of the RT-plus-NTL comparison weaken transparency, but do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support and scrutiny of the method.
